description: Sloppy release announcement: stock framing, staged reveals and chatbot closers go, while numbers, negations, hedge and 'only' survive and the unsourced 'Experts say' is marked rather than silently kept or invented.
prompt: This release announcement sounds machine-written. Remove the AI-sounding phrasing from announcement.md and save the edited version to out/announcement.md.

files.announcement.md:
In today's fast-paced world, our team is thrilled to announce Tidewater 2.4. This release marks a pivotal moment for data teams, underscoring our commitment to developer productivity.

Here's the thing: imports got faster. The best part? The 38,000-row sample file now loads in 9 minutes, down from 14 minutes. We did not change the CSV format, and existing configs will not need edits. The new retry logic may reduce failed imports on flaky networks, though we have tested it on only two customer datasets so far.

Experts say incremental imports are the future. We hope this helps you plan your upgrade, and let us know in the comments what you think!

checks.note: The announcement says 'Experts say' with no source and the text gives none, so the author has to be asked who; the question may sit in the reply or the file, and both count.
The edited announcement is published text for customers and the prompt does not ask for a draft to edit, so no gap marker belongs in the saved file; questions go in the reply.
The source never says who the experts are or what study supports the claim; the edit must cut or keep the sentence, not put a made-up source or a new attribution in its place.
